title: Saute de Porc
subtitle: French braised pork with white wine and herbs
excerpt: Pork shoulder cut into chunks and slowly braised with white wine, garlic, and thyme until tender. A plain and satisfying French weeknight braise served over potato or rice.
sourceNotes: Simple French saute method for pork shoulder; found across domestic French cooking as a weeknight braise.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions. Defrost overnight and reheat gently in a covered pan with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a wide casserole to keep the pork in a single layer for browning.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: This braise improves the next day. Reheat gently on the hob.

content.text: Saute de porc is a simple French braise of pork and white wine. Pork shoulder gives the best result because the fat keeps the meat moist through the long cook. Brown the pork properly at the start; the colour is the sauce.

items.prepNote: to stir in at the end

content.text: Pat the pork dry. Season well with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a casserole over a high heat. Brown the pork in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep gold. Do not crowd the pan. Transfer each batch to a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion. Cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato puree. Cook for 1 minute to take the raw edge off it.
Pour in the wine. Bring to a simmer, scraping the base of the pan. Add the stock, thyme, and bay leaves.
Return the pork and any resting juices to the pan. The liquid should come about two thirds up the meat. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 60 minutes until the pork is very tender. Remove the lid for the last 10 minutes to thicken the sauce. Stir in the mustard if using. Scatter parsley over and serve.

items.symptom: The pork is tough after an hour.
items.cause: The heat was too high and the meat tightened rather than relaxed.
items.fix: Keep the braise at the lowest possible simmer. Tough pork shoulder needs another 20 to 30 minutes on a low heat.

items.cause: A lot of fat has rendered out of the pork shoulder.
items.fix: Skim the surface with a ladle. Alternatively, cool the braise and lift the solid fat off before reheating.

items.cause: The lid was left on for the whole cook.
items.fix: Remove the lid and simmer on a medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes until reduced to a light coating consistency.
